_link.title: I can explain that electric fields change the speed of charged particles while magnetic fields change their direction

toLevel2.stem: What effect does an electric field have on a charged particle?
distractors: It changes only the particle's direction
It has no effect on the particle at all
It changes the particle's mass value

toLevel2.stem: What effect does a magnetic field have on a moving charged particle?
distractors: It changes the particle's speed value
It increases the particle's mass value
It has no effect on the particle at all

toLevel2.stem: In a particle accelerator, which type of field is used to accelerate particles to higher speeds?
distractors: A magnetic field
A gravitational field
A thermal radiation field

toLevel2.stem: In a particle accelerator, which type of field is used to steer particles along a curved path?
distractors: An electric field
A gravitational field
A frictional contact field

toLevel2.stem: Why does a magnetic field not change the speed of a charged particle?
toLevel2.answer: The magnetic force is perpendicular to the velocity so it does no work
distractors: The magnetic force is too weak to affect the particle's kinetic energy
The magnetic field cancels out the particle's kinetic energy completely
The magnetic force acts parallel to the velocity but in the opposite way

toLevel2.stem: Electric fields change a particle's {{blank:1}}, while magnetic fields change a particle's {{blank:2}}.
In a synchrotron, {{blank:1}} fields accelerate the particles and {{blank:2}} fields bend the beam into a circular path.
The electric force can do {{blank:1}} on a charged particle because it acts along the direction of {{blank:2}}.
A magnetic field can be used to increase the speed of a charged particle.
distractors: True

toLevel2.stem: An electric field does work on a charged particle, changing its kinetic energy.
distractors: False

toLevel3.stem: Why does the electric force change a particle's speed while the magnetic force does not?
toLevel3.answer: The electric force has a component along the velocity (doing work), while the magnetic force is always perpendicular (doing no work)
distractors: The electric force is always stronger than the magnetic force on any charged particle
The magnetic force only exists for a short time so it cannot change the speed significantly
The electric force acts on the charge directly while the magnetic force acts on the mass

toLevel3.stem: In the Australian Synchrotron, why are both electric and magnetic fields necessary?
toLevel3.answer: Electric fields provide the energy to reach high speeds; magnetic fields keep the beam on a circular path
distractors: Electric fields provide direction control while magnetic fields provide the energy input
Both fields provide acceleration; using two types is faster than using one type alone
Electric fields are used for electrons while magnetic fields are used for protons only

toLevel3.stem: A charged particle enters a region with only a magnetic field. Which statement is true about the particle's kinetic energy?
toLevel3.answer: The kinetic energy remains constant because the magnetic force does no work
distractors: The kinetic energy increases because the magnetic force accelerates the particle
The kinetic energy decreases because the magnetic force decelerates the particle
The kinetic energy oscillates because the force direction keeps changing constantly

toLevel3.stem: How does the concept of work explain the difference between electric and magnetic fields in accelerators?
toLevel3.answer: Work requires a force component along the displacement; electric forces have this component but magnetic forces do not
distractors: Work is only done by electric fields because magnetic fields are not real physical forces
Both fields do work on charged particles but the magnetic work is absorbed by the field
Work is done by both fields equally but the magnetic work converts to heat instead

toLevel3.stem: A student suggests using a magnetic field alone to build a particle accelerator. Why would this not work?
toLevel3.answer: Magnetic fields cannot increase the kinetic energy of particles, so they cannot accelerate them to higher speeds
distractors: Magnetic fields are too expensive to produce at the strength needed for acceleration
Magnetic fields would demagnetise the particles making them unable to respond to forces
Magnetic fields can only accelerate neutral particles, not charged particles like electrons

toLevel3.stem: In a linear accelerator (linac), particles pass through a series of accelerating gaps. What type of field exists in each gap?
toLevel3.answer: An electric field that does work on the particles and increases their speed
distractors: A magnetic field that curves the particles through each gap in the accelerator
Both electric and magnetic fields working together to steer and speed particles
A gravitational field that pulls the particles through each gap in succession

toLevel3.stem: Work equals force times {{blank:1}} in the direction of the force. The magnetic force is {{blank:2}} to the displacement, so it does no work.
A linear accelerator uses {{blank:1}} fields in the gaps to increase speed, while a synchrotron uses {{blank:2}} fields in the bending sections to maintain the circular path.
The key distinction is that electric fields change {{blank:1}} energy while magnetic fields change only the {{blank:2}} of the velocity vector.
In a synchrotron, the magnetic fields in the bending sections increase the speed of the particles.
distractors: True

toLevel4.stem: A proton passes through an electric field that accelerates it, then enters a magnetic field. Describe the energy changes in each region.
toLevel4.answer: In the electric field the proton gains kinetic energy; in the magnetic field its kinetic energy remains constant
distractors: In both fields the proton gains kinetic energy because both fields exert forces on it
In the electric field energy remains constant; in the magnetic field energy increases
In both fields the proton loses kinetic energy because the forces oppose its motion

toLevel4.stem: In a synchrotron, electrons lose energy by emitting synchrotron radiation as they are deflected by magnetic fields. How is this energy loss compensated?
toLevel4.answer: Electric fields in RF cavities restore the lost energy each revolution
distractors: The magnetic fields supply the lost energy directly from their own stored energy
The electrons naturally regain energy from the vacuum as they travel around the ring
Energy loss does not occur because magnetic fields cannot remove energy from particles

toLevel4.stem: A charged particle enters a region where electric and magnetic fields are both present and perpendicular to each other. The particle travels in a straight line. What can be concluded?
toLevel4.answer: The electric and magnetic forces are balanced, meaning the speed change from the electric force is offset by deflection prevention
distractors: Both fields are too weak to affect the particle so it continues in a straight line
The particle has no charge so neither field can exert any force on it in this region
The fields cancel each other out completely leaving no net field in the region at all

toLevel4.stem: An electron is fired through a uniform magnetic field and then through a uniform electric field of equal force magnitude. Compare the exit speeds.
toLevel4.answer: The speed after the magnetic field is unchanged; the speed after the electric field is different (higher or lower depending on direction)
distractors: Both fields produce the same final speed because the force magnitudes are equal
The magnetic field produces a higher exit speed because it acts for a longer time
The electric field leaves speed unchanged while the magnetic field changes the speed

toLevel4.stem: In a cyclotron, particles are accelerated by electric fields in the gap between the dees and curved by magnetic fields within the dees. Why must the electric field alternate?
toLevel4.answer: The particle crosses the gap twice per revolution, and the field must accelerate it each time by reversing direction
distractors: The alternating field prevents the particle from overheating inside the cyclotron dees
The alternating field creates a magnetic effect that helps steer the particle correctly
The alternating field is needed because DC fields cannot accelerate particles at all

toLevel4.stem: A student claims that because magnets can pick up iron objects, magnetic fields must do work. Analyse this claim in the context of charged particles.
toLevel4.answer: For charged particles the magnetic force is always perpendicular to velocity; the situation with iron involves induced magnetic dipoles which is a different mechanism
distractors: The student is correct; magnetic fields always do work on all objects including particles
The student is wrong; magnets do not actually pick up iron because they exert no real force
The claim proves that magnetic fields do work on charged particles just as they do on iron

toLevel4.stem: In a mass spectrometer, particles are first accelerated by an electric field then separated by a magnetic field. Why is this order essential?
toLevel4.answer: The electric field gives particles a known kinetic energy; the magnetic field then separates them by mass without changing their speed
distractors: The magnetic field must come second because it can only act on particles that are already fast
The electric field must come first because it determines the charge of each particle type
The order does not matter; both arrangements produce identical separation of the particles

toLevel4.stem: In a cyclotron, the {{blank:1}} field in the gap does work on the particle each crossing, while the {{blank:2}} field in the dees only changes direction.
Synchrotron radiation causes energy {{blank:1}}, which is compensated by {{blank:2}} fields in RF cavities.
The electric field is responsible for {{blank:1}} while the magnetic field is responsible for {{blank:2}} in particle accelerators.

toLevel5.stem: Evaluate why the distinction between electric and magnetic field roles is fundamental to the design of every modern particle accelerator.
toLevel5.answer: Without this distinction, engineers could not independently control particle speed and direction, which is essential for beam management
distractors: The distinction is a theoretical convenience but has no practical impact on accelerator design
Modern accelerators use only magnetic fields; the distinction is relevant only historically
The distinction matters only for electrons; proton accelerators use a single unified field

toLevel5.stem: A student proposes that at relativistic speeds, the distinction between electric and magnetic fields breaks down because they transform into each other. Evaluate this claim for accelerator design.
toLevel5.answer: While fields do transform between frames in relativity, in the lab frame the functional distinction (speed vs direction) remains valid for design purposes
distractors: The claim is wrong; electric and magnetic fields never transform into each other under any conditions
The claim means accelerators cannot work at relativistic speeds because fields become identical
The claim is correct and means all accelerators must use only one type of field at high speeds

toLevel5.stem: Compare a synchrotron and a linear accelerator in terms of how each uses electric and magnetic fields.
toLevel5.answer: Both use electric fields for acceleration, but the synchrotron also needs magnetic fields to bend the beam into a circle; a linac travels straight so needs minimal steering
distractors: A linac uses only magnetic fields while a synchrotron uses only electric fields for operation
Both use identical configurations of electric and magnetic fields throughout their structures
A linac uses magnetic fields for acceleration while a synchrotron uses electric fields instead

toLevel5.stem: Analyse why synchrotron radiation is an unavoidable consequence of using magnetic fields to steer high-energy electrons.
toLevel5.answer: Accelerating charges emit radiation; the centripetal acceleration from the magnetic force causes energy loss as electromagnetic radiation
distractors: Synchrotron radiation occurs because the magnetic field directly converts electron mass into light
Synchrotron radiation is caused by the electric fields in the RF cavities, not the magnetic fields
Synchrotron radiation is avoidable by using stronger magnetic fields to reduce the acceleration

toLevel5.stem: In a velocity selector, electric and magnetic forces are balanced for a specific speed. Predict what happens to a particle moving faster than this selected speed.
toLevel5.answer: The magnetic force exceeds the electric force, deflecting the particle out of the straight path
distractors: The electric force exceeds the magnetic force, deflecting the particle in the opposite way
Both forces increase equally so the particle continues in a straight line at higher speed
The particle slows down to the selected speed because the net force opposes its motion

toLevel5.stem: A physicist wants to store a beam of particles in a ring for hours. Which field type is most important for this purpose, and why?
toLevel5.answer: Magnetic fields, because they can maintain the circular path without changing particle speed, preserving beam energy
distractors: Electric fields, because they are needed to keep the particles moving at constant speed
Both fields equally, because without constant acceleration the particles would stop naturally
Neither field, because particles in a vacuum continue moving in circles without any force

toLevel5.stem: Evaluate why proton accelerators can reach higher energies than electron accelerators of the same ring size.
toLevel5.answer: Protons lose far less energy to synchrotron radiation because radiation loss scales inversely with mass to the fourth power
distractors: Protons have a higher charge so the electric fields can do more work on them per revolution
Protons are heavier so they require less magnetic field strength to maintain the circular path
Electrons are lighter and therefore cannot be contained by the magnetic fields at high energies

toLevel5.stem: Compare the roles of electric and magnetic fields in a medical linear accelerator used for cancer treatment.
toLevel5.answer: Electric fields accelerate electrons or X-ray-producing targets to high energy; magnetic fields steer and focus the beam onto the tumour
distractors: Only electric fields are used because medical linacs do not contain any magnetic components
Only magnetic fields are used because electric fields would damage the patient's tissue cells
Both fields work identically to destroy cancer cells through direct electromagnetic interaction

toLevel5.stem: Proton accelerators reach higher energies than electron accelerators because protons lose far less energy to {{blank:1}} radiation due to their greater {{blank:2}}.
Storage rings use {{blank:1}} fields to maintain the beam path and periodic {{blank:2}} fields to compensate for energy losses.
